instruction: Add a BLUE color constant with value (0, 0, 255) to the Snake game's settings file, alongside the existing color definitions.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened VS Code with Snake game project, browsed all 4 files (food.py, main.py, settings.py, snake.py), correctly identified the code structure, attempted Find & Replace to fix collision detection, then tried adding a @property to snake.py but introduced IndentationError. Ran python3 main.py, got IndentationError. Spent remaining 50 turns debugging indentation without resolving.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate VS Code file explorer, open files, read and understand Python code, open terminal, run shell commands, install packages via pip, use Find & Replace dialog
metadata.failure_analysis: Model correctly identified the bug direction but struggled with precise text editing in VS Code. Added a @property but broke indentation. Could not recover from the IndentationError despite multiple attempts.
metadata.task_rationale: Slightly harder than a value change: requires adding a new line in settings.py. The model demonstrated ability to navigate to settings.py and understand its structure. Adding a line is simpler than the multi-file bug fix of the original task.
metadata.explanation: Task requires adding a BLUE color constant (0, 0, 255) to settings.py. Getter runs python3 to execute settings.py and print BLUE. Metric checks if BLUE equals (0, 0, 255).

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly executes settings.py and prints the BLUE variable, then parses the tuple output into an RGB list — accurately extracts the required state
Metric correctly handles the expected parameter (directly accesses expected.get('expected_rgb')) consistent with get_rule returning the rules dict
Metric comparison logic (list equality) is appropriate for exact RGB value matching
Postconfig properly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before the getter reads it, ensuring state freshness
Complete coverage: the single instruction requirement (BLUE constant with value (0, 0, 255)) is fully verified
Error handling is adequate — returns defined=False on failure, metric returns 0.0 for error cases
